findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand sink next to the dish area to have a gradual leak from the waste line. A plumber responded last week, but the leak persists. Ensure the plumber returns to repair the sink and all wastewater is surveyed properly to prevent cross-contamination. Inspector will follow up again on July 16, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored above pots of soup in the walk-in cooler. Staff were informed and the eggs were moved to a shelf above raw chicken. Education was conducted with the PIC regarding proper storage order practices, and a handout in Chinese and English was provided. Ensure proper storage order is followed at all times to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine as well as the counter surrounding the ice basin of the soda machine to be heavily soiled with microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to contact a service representative for professional cleaning. A follow-up will be conducted on July 20, 2026 to ensure the ice machine and ice basin of the soda machine is clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish machine in the kitchen to measure 0ppm chlorine with a test strip. The PIC was informed and discovered that the bucket of chemical attached to the machine was empty. The bucket was replaced and the machine was cycled multiple times to prime the chemical. Chemical was not detected after multiple cycles. A follow up will be conducted on July 13, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a slow wastewater leak from the plumbing below the hand sink near the dish area. The PIC was informed and stated that the leak must be new, as she has not noticed it in the past. The basin of the sink was observed slow to drain. Inspector recommends contacting a professional plumber for repair. A follow-up will be conducted on July 13, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the triple sink and mop sink in the kitchen to have damaged silicone sealant between the sinks and the wall. The sealant was observed both cracked/damaged and soiled with microbial growth. Ensure staff remove the existing sealant and replace it with new silicone to make the surface smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. This repair needs to be completed prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed rice and rice noodles soaking in buckets with no lid stored directly on the floor. The PIC was advised to keep food containers covered at all times as well as at least 6 inches off the ground. Coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container. The PIC placed covers on both buckets and moved them to a counter during the inspection. This violation is considered corrected on site. 

The inspector recommends investing in additional shelving or carts for buckets to avoid this violation in the future.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed knives in the bar area to be stored between the prep cooler and the counter. This are is not accessible for cleaning/sanitizing, and therefore is not safe for utensil storage. The knives were moved to the dish area during the inspection. Ensure the knives are stored on an easily cleanable surface to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

Coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container.  The PIC placed covers on both buckets during the inspection. This violation is considered corrected on site.

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed riceice and rice noodles soaking in water in buckets on the floor. Advised to store elsewhere on a shelf or table. Never store open containers of food on the floor to prevent contamination. Staff moved rice and noodles off floor during the inspection. This violation is considered corrected-on-site.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: PIC had copies of the employee health reporting agreements, but they were not signed. Advised that all employees need to sign the agreement and the signed copies should be kept in records. This form advises employees that if they are experiencing any of the symptoms mentioned, they should not handle food or food services, and should not come into work. Follow-up is scheduled for 2/27/25 to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Repeat - Observed employee place soiled fruit storage container in bar handwashing sink. Food debris observed in kitchen handwashing sink. Advised that handwashing sinks are for washing hands ONLY, no dumping of food waste or cleaning equipment allowed in handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed cut lettuce, curry sauces, and dry noodles stored with no lid. Advised to keep food containers covered at all times. Regardless of the food being stored in a fridge or freezer, coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container.  Follow-up is scheduled for 2/27/25 to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
The following food storage/contamination violations were observed in the kitchen: 
1. Rice and rice noodles soaking in water in buckets on the floor. Advised to store elsewhere on a shelf or table. Never store open containers of food on the floor to prevent contamination. Staff moved rice and noodles off floor.
2. Raw beef stored in the deli cooler above open container of cut iceberg lettuce. Advised that the juices from the beef could drip into the lettuce, resulting in contamination. Always store raw meat at the lowest shelf, and produce above. Storage order was fixed immediately.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Observed wiping cloths used for cleaning food surfaces stored on food prep surfaces. Advised cook staff to store sanitizing cloths in sanitizer (water and bleach). This helps keep cloths clean and sanitized between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed soup and rice bowls stored with food contact surface exposed to potential contamination. Advised cook staff to store dishes upside down on a clean surface or to cover to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed fan covering in walk-in cooler to be soiled with dust/debris. Clean cooler with enough frequency to ensure no build-up of dust and debris. Dust from the fans can be blown in to soup pots/other containers in the cooler and contaminate food.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed utensils in basin of bar hand sink. Utensil was removed during inspection. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed scoops used to dispense flour in kitchen to be heavily soiled with food debris. Scoops were removed and cleaned and sanitized during inspection.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed wet mop heads to be stored head down in mop bucket. Store wet mop heads in a fashion that promotes quick drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
